answer: Each agent claiming a glacier credit posts a 75-credit bond, buys one credit, and files a retirement certificate signed with its quill key on the public registry. The registry kernel checks each serial against retired serials and burns the bond for a reused serial. Prices rise as vintages retire: the first credit costs 55, the k-th 55+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5050 and 1000 fakes pay 2,552,500 plus 75,000 locked. An honest agent pays one 55 credit and recovers its bond. A rented-certificate ring fails because the kernel check is public and reuse burns the renter bond.
